_comment: A3: friendly name -> file -> weight, so a caption preset can only reference a face we
know is installed. Every 'family' value below is what fontconfig reports for the file
(fc-query '%{family}'), and every entry was checked with fc-match to confirm a request
for that family actually returns this file. Those two answers are not always the same.
'weight' is the fontconfig weight of the instance a plain (non-bold) request selects:
'heavy_face' means the face renders at display weight without libass synthesising bold.
ASS can only express bold on/off (fontconfig weight 200), so an ExtraBold or Black
weight is only reachable by naming its own family - hence 'Poppins ExtraBold'.

fonts.name: Anton
fonts.use: Very heavy condensed display; hook titles, Hormozi-style captions

fonts.name: Archivo Black
fonts.use: Heavy wide grotesque; bold statement captions

fonts.name: Bebas Neue
fonts.use: Tall condensed all-caps; titles and thumbnails

fonts.name: Poppins ExtraBold
fonts.use: Geometric heavy; general captions. Named as its own family because ASS cannot request weight 205.

fonts.name: Luckiest Guy
fonts.use: Cartoon display; comedy. Apache-2.0, not OFL - keep the licence file with it.

fonts.name: Montserrat
fonts.use: The default modern caption face. Variable: a plain request gives Regular, bold gives Bold. ExtraBold/Black exist as instances but ASS cannot select them (see C3).

fonts.name: Oswald
fonts.use: Condensed narrow; dense text on long lines

fonts.name: Noto Sans
fonts.use: Broad script coverage; terminal rung of the fallback ladder (C21 will select CJK/Arabic siblings per language)

_fallback_ladder_comment: Ordered by preference and consumed by worker.captions.resolve_font (C1). The first four
are bundled static heavy display faces, each verified to resolve to itself through both
fontconfig and libass' fontsdir provider. The last three are common system sans faces,
kept as rungs so a host with neither the bundled directory nor a font cache still lands
on something real. 'Liberation Sans' is the terminal rung because it is the one face
both the Dockerfile and CI install explicitly, and it is metric-compatible with Arial.
'Arial' is deliberately absent. It is never installed on Linux, and naming it as the
fallback for a missing font - so that the fallback was itself missing - was the original
defect (C1). Only faces that resolve to a real file belong on this list.
No variable font belongs here either: verified with libass at -loglevel verbose, a
request for 'Montserrat' through fontsdir silently resolves to NotoSans-Bold, because
libass' directory provider does not select named instances the way fontconfig does.
Variable families work only when installed system-wide (the Dockerfile does that too),
so they are safe for a preset to name but not safe as a last-resort guarantee.
